articles.title: Mexican soccer banned promotion and relegation. Senators may bring it back
articles.summary: Mexican leagues stopped pro/rel in 2020 due to Covid-19. Promised return in 2025 has not materialized. The debate over the absence of promotion and relegation in Mexican soccer has reached the floor of the country’s Senate, where officials announced that a legislative reform to restore the system…
body: Senator Clemente Castañeda of the Movimiento Ciudadano party put forward the proposal, backed by representatives from other party leaderships, including Ignacio Mier of the ruling Morena party.

Castañeda stated that the initiative is critical for “expressly incorporating sporting merit among the obligations that national sports associations must observe” and ensuring promotion and relegation are enshrined in Mexican law.

“When they closed off the possibility of promotion, they didn’t just change a sporting rule; they also restricted a path for players, staff, and sports projects to grow in a country that needs to open up opportunities,” Castañeda said.
The senator said that she invited the president of the Liga MX, Francisco Iturbide, and the commissioner of the Mexican football, Mikel Arriola, and they declined.

articles.title: Great Britain exit Billie Jean King Cup to mighty Czechia in quarter-finals
articles.summary: Defeats for Kartal and Boulter condemn Britain to loss. Men will play Germany in quarter-finals of Davis Cup. Great Britain’s stay at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals lasted only one match as they fell to Czechia in the quarter-finals in Shenzhen.
body: Led by Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, the whole Czech team is ranked higher than any of Britain’s players, and it was Noskova who sealed victory with a 6-2, 7-6 (3) win over Boulter. That followed a lengthy struggle between Marie Bouzkova and Kartal lasting a minute short of three hours, which the Czech eventually took 7-6 (2) 4-6 6-4.

It was a fine effort from Kartal, who was playing her first match in six months after suffering a stress fracture in her back in Indian Wells in March and she will now hope to finish the season strongly. The Czechs will bid for their seventh title in the competition since 2011 while Britain’s hopes of lifting the trophy for the first time are over for another year.

Keothavong’s team have over-performed in the Billie Jean King Cup in recent years and did so again by reaching the finals, with an under-strength team upsetting Australia in April. Neither Kartal nor Boulter were available for that tie, with the former in the early stages of an injury break that would eventually see her miss the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open.

articles.title: Rams crush Giants but Jaxson Dart escapes ‘devastating outcome’ after knee injury
articles.summary: New York Giants 6-28 Los Angeles Rams. Aaron Donald celebrates return to NFL with victory. Davante Adams has eight catches for 195 yards. Davante Adams made eight catches for 195 yards and hauled in two of Matthew Stafford’s four touchdown passes, and the Los Angeles Rams welcomed Aaron Donald back…
body: Stafford passed for 327 yards for the Rams (1-1), who capitalized after the Giants (1-1) lost Jaxson Dart to a knee injury on their first offensive series.

The Rams played without injured All-Pros Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett, but Stafford and Adams put on a vintage performance as the preseason Super Bowl favorites rebounded from their 27-7 debacle of a loss to the 49ers in Australia.

Adams’s catches and yards receiving were his best in a Rams uniform, while reigning MVP Stafford moved into sixth place in NFL history with his 426th career TD pass. He moved past Philip Rivers when Adams adroitly tracked down an 11-yard fade in the third quarter.

Jameis Winston replaced Dart and went 11 of 27 for 111 yards with an interception. Dart left the field after taking a huge hit from Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart on New York’s seventh play. The second-year quarterback, who looked great in last week’s win over Dallas, watched the second half in a track suit while the Giants managed just 182 yards of offense compared to LA’s 481. ESPN reported that Dart sprained his MCL and will miss playing time, but he is not believed to have broken any bones. He will undergo an MRI on Tuesday.

articles.title: La Liga president says Real Madrid conspiracy claims are ‘in another galaxy’
articles.summary: ‘The competition belongs to no one,’ says Javier Tebas. President hits out after Mourinho’s reaction to derby loss. La Liga’s president, Javier Tebas, hit out on Tuesday at what he deemed accusations of a refereeing “conspiracy” by Real Madrid after their derby defeat against Atlético Madrid.
body: Real Madrid’s coach, José Mourinho, brought two printed screenshots of what he thought were red-card tackles committed by Atéltico players to his post-match press conference after the 2-1 defeat on Sunday.
Tebas responded to a pro-Real article on social media with a lengthy riposte to allegations of a “conspiracy” against the 15-time European champions.

“Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative – the permanent conspiracy,” said Tebas, who has often been at odds with Real Madrid and the club’s outspoken president, Florentino Pérez.

“This article goes further – it claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’. What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership, or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.

articles.title: GB out of BJK Cup as Kartal & Boulter beaten by Czechs
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter lose their singles matches as Great Britain are beaten by a strong Czech Republic side in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals.
body: Anne Keothavong's team headed into the tie as underdogs, with all five Czech players placed higher in the singles rankings than any of the British squad.

Sonay Kartal produced a gritty performance as she returned to tennis after six months out with a lower back injury, but fell to a narrow 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 6-4 defeat in a marathon three-hour encounter with Marie Bouzkova.
Boulter could do little to get Britain back into the best-of-three tie as she was outplayed 6-2 7-6 (7-3) by Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.
It was a second successive loss for Boulter at the hands of a Czech player, coming just three weeks after a 58-minute demolition by Karolina Muchova at the US Open.

articles.title: Who will start for England at Euro 2028? BBC Sport's predictions
articles.summary: As England prepare to face world champions Spain on Saturday, BBC Sport's experts predict who will be starting for the Three Lions at Euro 2028.
body: Less than two months after Spain were celebrating their World Cup triumph, the next major tournament cycle begins.
From 9 June 2028, the European Championship will be hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland - and the path to the finals starts now.

England host Spain on Saturday in their Nations League opener and, while the competition doesn't offer a direct qualification route, it does provide a secondary route for teams who don't qualify automatically.
Despite being co-hosts of Euro 2028, Thomas Tuchel's men are not guaranteed a spot in the tournament - with all hosts having to earn their place.

articles.summary: We have reached Week 3, and it is time to set our lineups. The last thing you want is to end up with a dud in your lineup, especially in your running back slot. Despite having to go up against the Bears' rushing attack, the Vikings have allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy points to running backs at just 11.9 points per game. We are very concerned about Irving this week, along with everyone in the Buccaneers' offense.

articles.title: Pollock left money on table to stay at Saints - Hearn
articles.summary: Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth much more than his Northampton extension, which will earn him over £400,000 a year, says adviser Eddie Hearn.
body: Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth hundreds of thousands of pounds more than his extension to stay at boyhood club Northampton, says Eddie Hearn.
Hearn, whose Matchroom promotional empire is centred on boxing, darts and snooker, has been working as Pollock's adviser since March.
Pollock, 21, has agreed a new deal with Saints that extends his terms to summer 2028 and is worth more than £400,000 a year.
"There were a couple of domestic offers – a couple of Prem offers - and international offers as well," said Hearn of Pollock's options during his renegotiation.

articles.title: Clemson, Georgia Cancel 4-Game Series in Football
articles.summary: Clemson and Georgia have mutually agreed to cancel the upcoming 4 game series between the two schools according to reporting by the Athens Banner-Herald. The news was discovered via an open records request this week, though the agreement was signed back in March.
body: This news isn’t that surprising. Clemson entered into a 12 year agreement with Notre Dame followed by the ACC announcing a move to 9 conference games each year. Clemson’s annual rivalry against South Carolina and the inherent desire to play a cupcake to get 7 home games meant any other P4 out of conference games were unlikely. Somehow teams are allergic to playing 12 P4 games.

Frankly this sucks. As we talked about when the Notre Dame series was announced, these moves now are all about money. The Notre Dame series is nice, but Clemson – Notre Dame doesn’t have the tradition of Clemson – UGA or a host of other potential OOC matchups. Clemson “needs” 7 home games a year, that’s impossible to do with all P4 OOC opponents, especially in years when Clemson will only have 4 home conference games.

At this point it is hard to say when, if ever, Clemson will play UGA again. Until there are drastic changes in conference scheduling, or the Notre Dame series is cancelled, the powers that be won’t see space in the schedule for UGA. And it is a real shame. The recent revival of this series was great and something that should remain in college football.

articles.summary: The raw emotion caught on tape in the first quarter was just a preview of how Caitlin Clark really felt about Indiana’s performance. The Washington Mystics completely blew past Indiana 93–77, snapping the Fever’s three-game win streak before it could really take off.
body: Frustrated by the defensive lapses, head coach Stephanie White started pulling levers on her rotation, handing rookie Raven Johnson 26 minutes to spark some energy while cutting Sophie Cunningham 's playing time down to single digits.
With Washington's offense slicing through Indiana's defense early on, broadcast mics caught Caitlin Clark visibly fuming toward what appeared to be head coach Stephanie White.
Throwing her hand up in pure frustration, Clark demanded better help coverage on the court, shouting: "That's why we need to rotate, so it's not everyone for themselves!"

Speaking in the postgame presser after the loss, she was asked by a reporter: "It looked like there was a lot of frustration from basically everybody in that first quarter. I mean, what would you describe as some of the things that went wrong?"

articles.title: Why did Tom Brady want the Raiders? Maybe this is why
articles.summary: As I walked out of Allegiant Stadium in the middle of last November, following the Las Vegas Raiders' miserable home defeat to the Dallas Cowboys, I looked at all the downcast fans trudging away and I thought, why does Tom Brady want to be involved with this?
body: As many of you know, the seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback has a top front office job with the Raiders, as well as being a TV commentator, and it's his job to try to build the silver and black back into a contender. But they felt miles away from contention on that night in November.

They'd just lost 33-16 to the Cowboys, Geno Smith was ineffective a quarterback and arguing with fans in the stands, star defensive end Max Crosby was so frustrated at the final gun that he launched his helmet about 40 yards across the field.

That stadium in Las Vegas is nicknamed the Death Star, and as I walked away that night, I was reminded of the very first Star Wars film and thought, like the original Death Star, this thing needs to be blown up. Not the stadium, but the football program.

articles.title: Blake Miller injury: Lions OT 'trending the right way,' Campbell says
articles.summary: Offensive tackle Blake Miller probably could have played against the Buffalo Bills had the Lions had a full week to rest and recover from their season opener, Coach Dan Campbell said on the "Costa & Jansen with Heather" show Tuesday, Sept. 22 on 97.1 The Ticket.
body: Miller never missed a game in his college career but was sidelined for the team's 41-31 loss on Thursday, Sept. 17 with a knee injury. Miller said early in the week that he was "optimistic" about his chances of playing. Ultimately, there wasn't enough time for him to get right before Detroit traveled to Buffalo; he and left guard Christian Mahogany were ruled out on the team's game status report.

"Yeah, I think there's a good chance had it been Sunday, he'd have played," Campbell said on the radio. "I feel pretty good that he's trending the right way to be in there, but (we) won't know until we get him out there on the field."
Campbell added that the plan is to have Mahogany back to practice on Wednesday, Sept. 23.

Despite eventually finishing with 31 points, the Lions ' offense looked like a fish out of water early on in the matchup against Buffalo, running just seven plays on their first two drives as the Bills raced out to a 21-0 lead before Detroit found the end zone. Reserve right tackle Larry Borom allowed a whopping 11 pressures and two sacks, per Pro Football Focus; backup left guard Ben Bartch allowed six pressures.

articles.title: Webster: Littler won't walk away from darts over crowd treatment
articles.summary: Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster believes Luke Littler will not walk away from darts over crowd treatment, adding the PDC are determined to rid the sport of whistling but that boos will always remain.
body: Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the main talking point coming out of the event was Littler's continued fractious relationship with darts fans.
Indeed, earlier in the tournament Littler threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during victory over Nathan Aspinall.

The back-to-back world champion also faced a hostile environment during Friday's win over home favourite Danny Noppert and it escalated on Saturday night as referee Charlie Corstorphine had to intervene in the last-16 win over Aspinall.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there, but Webster does not believe Littler will leave the sport entirely over it.
